P1-3.notes: Reach the start notch by scrambling around the bergschrunds, about 100 ft above the base of the pyramid. The first pitch is class 3 on solid rock with good cracks for gear up to about 1.5 in; the next two are easy 4th class with horns for slings or terrain belays.

review.changed: Wrote P1-3 only (terrain split between class 3 and easy 4th, horns, crack protection, bergschrund scramble to the notch). P4-6 not in batch. Second page (SummitPost Southeast Corner) returned 403, so only one full page read.
review.other_findings: Search snippets disagree on difficulty of the upper pitches (5.3-5.4 vs a 5.6 report); the stored 5.6/5.7 crest-steps note is not confirmed by the page read.

Summit pitch.notes: The couloir tops out on the ridge. From there easy rock scrambling leads over to the NW Ridge, where a single 5.4 rock pitch reaches the summit. One party used a rappel anchor and downclimbed the rest on the way off.

review.changed: Wrote the summit pitch from one trip report; no length, gear or anchor details stated, so none added. The ski report read did not go to the summit.

Goat Flats to Tin Can Gap.notes: Mostly above treeline: follow the ridge above the flats until it steepens, then traverse right across a south-facing slope to the gap. Easy trail in summer; wet slides and cornices are a concern in winter and spring. The maintained trail effectively ends at the gap.

Tin Can Gap across the Queest-Alb Glacie.notes: Cross or skirt a small, steep snowfield on the north side of the ridge, then cross the ridge onto the south face and return north at the top of the glacier. Late summer, a moat between ice and rock can be followed. A slip near the glacier slides about 200 ft into rock, so carry an axe, and consider crampons and a rope. Ends at a snowfield below the summit rock.
